items.label: text
items.text: freezing point the temperature at which a substance changes its state from a liquid to a solid hydrocarbon molecules containing carbon and hydrogen only

items.label: text
items.text: fuela substance that when burned in oxygen releases heat energy

items.label: text
items.text: fume strong-smelling gas or smoke that is unpleasant to breathe in

items.label: text
items.text: functional group an atom or a group of atoms that determine the chemical properties of a compound

items.label: text
items.text: galvanisation a method of preventing rusting by coating iron with a layer of zinc

items.label: text
items.text: general formula a formula applicable to all members of a homologous series, for example CH2n+2 for alkanes and CH2for alkenes

items.label: text
items.text: giant a structure in which there are no individual molecules and the bonding extends in all directions. There is no limit to the number of particles present

items.label: text
items.text: giant ionic lattice the arrangement of ions in an ionic compound in its solid state

items.label: text
items.text: girder a strong beam, made of iron or steel, that supports a floor, roof or bridge

items.label: text
items.text: global warming greenhouse gases, including carbon dioxide, trap the heat radiated from the Earth's surface (originally from the Sun) and lead to an increase in the temperature of the Earth and its atmosphere

items.label: text
items.text: glowproduce a steady light

items.label: text
items.text: greenhouse gas gases such as carbon dioxide which can trap heat radiated from the Earth's surface (originally from the Sun)

items.label: text
items.text: group a vertical column in the Periodic Table. All elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons

items.label: text
items.text: half-equation a balanced symbol equation to describe either oxidation or reduction

items.label: text
items.text: halogen group 7 element, including fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine

items.label: text
items.text: hammeredbeen hit with a hammer to be forced into a particular shape

items.label: text
items.text: homologous series a series of compounds with similar chemical properties because they have the same functional group. Each member differs from the next by -CH2-. The members show a gradation in physical properties

items.label: text
items.text: hydratedcontaining water

items.label: text
items.text: hydration the addition of water molecules to an unsaturated molecule, for example converting ethene to ethanol hydrogen bonda special type of intermolecular force found between water molecules and in some other substances hydrogen halide compound formed between hydrogen and a halogen, with the formula HX where X stands for a halogen atom hydrogenation the addition of hydrogen molecules to an unsaturated molecule, for example converting ethene to ethane hydroxonium ion an ion formed when water accepts a proton from an acid. It has the formula H₃O+

items.label: text
items.text: incomplete combustion occurs when a hydrocarbon burns in insufficient oxygen. Water is still formed as a product, but carbon monoxide or carbon are formed instead of carbon dioxide

items.label: text
items.text: independent variable what you vary in an experiment.

items.label: text
items.text: indicator a substance that has different colours depending on the pH

items.label: text
items.text: inert unreactive

items.label: text
items.text: intermolecular force force of attraction between covalent molecules, much weaker than covalent bonds within the molecules

items.label: text
items.text: ion charged particle formed when an atom (or group of atoms) loses or gains electrons

items.label: text
items.text: ionic bonding strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another

items.label: text
items.text: ionise become an ion. Usually refers to losing electrons to become a positive ion

items.label: text
items.text: iron filings small pieces of iron that are used in some chemical experiments

items.label: text
items.text: isoelectronic having the same number of electrons

items.label: text
items.text: isotopes different atoms of the same element, with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons. Isotopes have the same chemical properties

items.label: text
items.text: kinetic energy a form of energy a substance possesses due to motion

items.label: text
items.text: lattice a regular array of particles

items.label: text
items.text: Liebig condensera piece of equipment used to condense gas to liquid in distillation

items.label: text
items.text: litre a unit for volume. One litre = one dm³

items.label: text
items.text: lump a mass of solid without a particular shape
